summary: Possible typosquat of @coral-xyz/anchor with unverified bundle behavior
details: Package name `@solana-labs/ancor` under the `@solana-labs` scope closely resembles the well-known Solana smart-contract framework `anchor` (published as `@coral-xyz/anchor`, formerly `@project-serum/anchor`), with `ancor` being a one-character deletion from `anchor`. The shipped bundle `lib/index.cjs.js` / `lib/index.esm.js` contains keyword co-occurrence patterns (require('child_process'), fetch/POST, https.get, ping) in a minified blob, but file-level tracing did not complete and the patterns alone cannot be distinguished from legitimate composition (e.g., a Solana RPC client making HTTP calls to user-configured endpoints). The combination of (a) name proximity to a top-tier Solana package, (b) use of an organizational scope (`@solana-labs`) that suggests official Solana Labs provenance, and (c) a minified bundle with network + child_process primitives that has not been semantically verified, warrants human review before allow/block. Reviewer should confirm publisher identity vs. the legitimate Solana Labs / Anza / Coral organizations and trace the network destinations in the bundle.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
